6º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 5

There was / there were

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Describe places in the past with there was and there were
  • Choose was (singular) or were (plural)
  • Make negatives and questions: there wasn't, Was there…?
  • Compare a place in the past and now
  • Distinguish there was and it was
  • Compare the past and the present with there used to be
  • Set the scene of a story with there was / there were
  • Describe Pompeii and life a hundred years ago

Para pensar

En español decimos «había un castillo» y «había muchos caballos», siempre con «había». En inglés, ¿se dice igual para uno que para muchos?

Explicación

1. From there is to there was

You already know there is and there are (hay): «There is a park near my house», «There are two cinemas in my town». To talk about the past we use there was and there were (había, hubo).

En castellano: «hay» pasa a ser «había». En inglés, el singular pasa a was y el plural a were, igual que el verbo to be: is → was, are → were.

2. There was: singular

Use there was with one thing (a / an / one) and with uncountable nouns (nombres incontables: water, food, snow, money): «There was a big storm last night», «There was an old tree in the square», «There was a lot of snow in the mountains».

The short form there's is only for the present. In the past we always write there was in full. En castellano: «había una tormenta», «había mucha nieve».

3. There were: plural

Use there were with two or more things: «There were twenty children in the classroom», «There were some beautiful shells on the beach», «There were lots of people at the concert».

Careful with the first noun in a list: «There was a table and two chairs» (the first noun is singular) but «There were two chairs and a table». En castellano: mira la palabra que va justo detrás para elegir was o were.

4. Negatives: there wasn't, there weren't

Negative: there wasn't (was not) and there weren't (were not). With plural and uncountable nouns we usually add any: «There wasn't a swimming pool», «There weren't any cars in 1800», «There wasn't any milk in the fridge».

We can also say there was no / there were no: «There were no mobile phones when my grandma was a child». En castellano: «no había móviles». Ojo: nunca uses dos negaciones juntas («weren't no»).

5. Questions and short answers

For questions we change the order: Was there…? and Were there…? «Was there a library in your school?» – «Yes, there was. / No, there wasn't». «Were there any dinosaurs in Spain?» – «Yes, there were!».

To ask about quantity: «How many people were there?» (countable) and «How much food was there?» (uncountable). En castellano: «¿Cuántas personas había?», «¿Cuánta comida había?».

6. There was or it was?

Many students confuse there was and it was. They are different:

  • There was / there were says that something existed or was in a place. It introduces something new: «There was a dog in the garden.» (Había un perro.)
  • It was describes something we already know, or talks about the weather, the time or a situation: «It was black and white.» «It was cold.» «It was nine o'clock.» «It was fantastic!»

We often use them together: first there was to present the thing, then it was to describe it:

  • «There was a cake on the table. It was delicious.»
  • «There were some kittens in the box. They were very small.»

En castellano decimos «había» para los dos números (había un perro, había dos perros), pero en inglés cambia: there was en singular y there were en plural. Y nunca decimos «It was a dog in the garden» para decir «había un perro».

7. My town in the past

We use there was / there were to describe places long ago: «A hundred years ago there weren't any supermarkets in my town. There was a small market in the square. There were lots of farms and there was a railway station. There wasn't any electricity in some houses».

Compare with today using there is / there are: «Now there is a big supermarket and there are two schools». Consejo: pregunta a tus abuelos cómo era su pueblo y escríbelo en inglés.

8. There used to be…

To compare a place in the past and now, we can use there used to be. It means that something existed in the past, for a long time, but it doesn't exist now:

  • «There used to be a cinema in my street. Now there is a supermarket.»
  • «There used to be lots of trees here. Now there are houses.»
  • «There didn't use to be a park in my town, but now there is a big one.»
  • «Did there use to be a castle here?» – «Yes, there did.»

Notice that there used to be is the same for singular and plural.

Ask your grandparents or older neighbours what your town or neighbourhood was like when they were children. Here are some questions:

  • Was there a school? Were there many shops?
  • What used to be in the place where your house is now?
  • Were there many cars? Was there a train station?

Then compare the past and the present in a table with two columns: Then and Now.

9. Telling a story

Stories often start with there was or there were to present the place and the characters: «Once upon a time there was a little dragon who lived in a cave. There were lots of treasures in the cave, but there wasn't anyone to play with».

We use it to describe a scene: «When we arrived at the party, there was music and there were balloons everywhere». En castellano: «Érase una vez un dragón…» se dice en inglés «Once upon a time there was a dragon…».

10. Setting the scene

Good stories often begin by setting the scene: describing the place, the time and the atmosphere before the action starts. There was and there were are perfect for this:

  • Time and place: «Once upon a time, there was a little village by a lake.»
  • People and animals: «There were children playing in the square, and there was an old man sitting on a bench.»
  • Sounds and atmosphere: «There was a strange silence. There wasn't any wind.»

A great trick is there was / there were + person + -ing, which shows an action happening in the scene: «There was a woman selling flowers.» «There were birds singing in the trees.»

You can also use adjectives and prepositions of place to paint a clear picture: «In the middle of the forest, there was a tall, dark tower. Next to it, there was a small, frozen pond.»

After setting the scene, start the action with the past simple and a word like suddenly: «Suddenly, a door opened…»

11. Reading: a school trip to a castle

Read Nerea's text: «Last Friday we visited a castle. It was very old. Many years ago, there were soldiers and horses there. There was a big kitchen with a huge fireplace, but there wasn't a bathroom! There were some secret tunnels under the castle. «Were there any ghosts?» asked Mario. «No, there weren't», said the guide. «But there was a very old cat!». We all laughed.»

How many times do you see there was? And there were?

12. Let's practise: memory game

Look at a picture of a room for one minute. Then close your eyes. Your partner asks: «Was there a lamp?», «How many books were there?». Answer: «Yes, there was», «There were three books». Who remembers more?

Then describe a place you visited: «In the zoo there were lions and there was a big aquarium». Consejo: antes de escribir was o were, mira si lo que viene detrás es uno, varios o incontable.

13. Pompeii: a town frozen in time

Almost 2,000 years ago, in the year 79 AD, there was a busy Roman town called Pompeii, near the city of Naples, in Italy. About 11,000 people lived there, near a big mountain called Vesuvius. Nobody knew it was a volcano.

In Pompeii, there were houses with beautiful paintings and mosaics, and there were shops, bakeries and street «fast-food» counters where people bought hot food. There was a big amphitheatre for shows and there were public baths. On the walls, there were lots of messages and drawings, like modern graffiti. At the entrance of one house, there was a mosaic of a dog with the words «Cave canem», which means «Beware of the dog»!

Then, one day, Vesuvius erupted. There was a huge cloud of ash and hot gas, and in a few hours the town was buried under metres of ash and stones. Pompeii disappeared.

More than 1,600 years later, in the 18th century, people started to dig and found the town almost exactly as it was. Today, millions of tourists walk along its streets every year, and archaeologists are still discovering new things.

Thanks to the ash, we know a lot about daily life in a Roman town: what people ate, how they decorated their homes, what games children played and even what jokes they wrote on the walls.

14. A hundred years ago

Imagine you could travel back in time to a Spanish town a hundred years ago, in the 1920s. What was different?

  • There weren't any televisions, computers or mobile phones. The first radio stations in Spain started in 1924, and only a few families had a radio.
  • There were very few cars. People walked a lot, rode horses or bicycles, and in cities there were trams.
  • In many villages, there wasn't running water at home. People got water from a fountain or a well.
  • There weren't any supermarkets. There were small shops and markets, and people bought food every day because many homes didn't have a fridge.
  • Many children didn't go to school for long: they had to help their families in the fields or at home.
  • But there were also lots of children playing in the street with spinning tops, marbles and skipping ropes.

Now think about the future: what will people say about our life in a hundred years? «A hundred years ago, there were mobile phones and petrol cars…»

There was / there were

Ejercicios

  1. Complete: «There ___ a big storm yesterday.»

  2. Complete: «There ___ ten pencils in my bag.»

  3. Complete: «There ___ much water in the river.» (negative)

  4. Make it negative: «There were some biscuits.»

  5. Make a question: «There was a museum in your town.»

  6. Short answer: «Were there any people?» (no)

  7. Ask with How many: «There were five boats.»

  8. Correct: «In 1900 it had no computers.»

  9. Translate: «Había un perro y dos gatos.»

  10. Write three sentences about your classroom in 1º of Primary.

  11. Choose: «(There was / It was) a big tree in the park. (There was / It was) very old.»

  12. Complete: «There ___ (be) two bakeries in my village.»

  13. In what year did Vesuvius erupt?

  14. What does «Cave canem» mean?

  15. Were there mobile phones a hundred years ago?

  16. Write two sentences with there used to be about your town.

  17. Correct: «There was many people at the concert.»

  18. Set the scene: write two sentences with there was / were + -ing.

  19. Make a question: «There used to be a castle here.»

  20. Name three things there were in Pompeii.

  21. Write the beginning of a story (five sentences) setting the scene with there was/were.

  22. Compare life a hundred years ago and now (four sentences).

  23. Explain the difference between «There was a party» and «It was a party».

  24. Interview an older person and write a «Then and now» table about your town.

Practica

  1. «There ___ a cat on the roof.»

    1. A) were
    2. B) was
    3. C) had

  2. «There ___ two cats on the roof.»

    1. A) was
    2. B) is
    3. C) were

  3. «There ___ any milk.»

    1. A) wasn't
    2. B) weren't
    3. C) isn't no

  4. «___ there a park in your town?»

    1. A) Were
    2. B) Did
    3. C) Was

  5. «Were there any shops?» – «No, ___.»

    1. A) there wasn't
    2. B) there weren't
    3. C) they weren't

  6. «How many children ___?»

    1. A) were there
    2. B) there were
    3. C) was there

  7. «Había» in English is…

    1. A) it had
    2. B) there was / there were
    3. C) there has

  8. «There ___ a lot of snow last winter.»

    1. A) were
    2. B) are
    3. C) was

  9. «There were ___ phones in 1850.»

    1. A) no
    2. B) not
    3. C) any no

  10. Present of «there were» is…

    1. A) there is
    2. B) there are
    3. C) there have

  11. «There ___ some old coins in the box.»

    1. A) was
    2. B) were
    3. C) it was

  12. «There used to be» is used for…

    1. A) future plans
    2. B) now
    3. C) past situations that changed

  13. «There was a man ___ the guitar.»

    1. A) plays
    2. B) playing
    3. C) played

  14. Pompeii is in…

    1. A) Italy
    2. B) Greece
    3. C) Spain

  15. The first radio stations in Spain started in…

    1. A) 1824
    2. B) 1994
    3. C) 1924

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué significan there was y there were; Cuándo se usa was y cuándo were; Cómo se hacen las negativas con any y no; Cómo se pregunta y se contesta con respuestas cortas.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

there wasHabía (una cosa o incontable).
there wereHabía (varias cosas).
there wasn'tNo había (singular).
there weren't anyNo había ningunos.
Was there…?¿Había…? (singular).
Were there…?¿Había…? (plural).
How many … were there?¿Cuántos … había?
Once upon a time there was…Érase una vez…
There was vs it wasThere was: something exists. It was: description, weather, time.
There used to bePast situation, not true now. Did there use to be…?
Setting the sceneThere was a woman selling flowers. There were birds singing.
Pompeii79 AD, Vesuvius; houses, bakeries, amphitheatre, graffiti.

Soluciones

  1. B) Una cosa: was.
  2. C) Plural: were.
  3. A) Incontable, negativa.
  4. C) Singular: Was there…?
  5. B) Respuesta corta.
  6. A) Orden de pregunta, plural.
  7. B) No se usa had.
  8. C) Snow es incontable.
  9. A) were no = no había.
  10. B) were → are.
  11. B) Plural.
  12. C) Used to.
  13. B) Setting the scene.
  14. A) Pompeii.
  15. C) 100 years ago.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. was.
  2. were.
  3. wasn't.
  4. There weren't any biscuits.
  5. Was there a museum in your town?
  6. No, there weren't.
  7. How many boats were there?
  8. In 1900 there were no computers.
  9. There was a dog and two cats.
  10. Model answer: There were lots of toys. There was a big carpet. There weren't any computers.
  11. There was; It was.
  12. were.
  13. In 79 AD.
  14. Beware of the dog.
  15. No, there weren't.
  16. Open answer.
  17. There were many people at the concert.
  18. Open answer. Example: There were children playing. There was a man selling ice creams.
  19. Did there use to be a castle here?
  20. Houses with mosaics, bakeries, an amphitheatre (also baths, graffiti).
  21. Open answer.
  22. Open answer.
  23. There was: a party existed/happened. It was a party: describes something already mentioned.
  24. Open answer.
